key_insight: Natural-language instructions can be translated into linear temporal logic (LTL) by answering predefined questions instead of generating text.
engineering_relevance: This approach supports on-device robot task translation with lower runtime and energy use, reducing reliance on cloud computation.
method: Decompose translation within a fixed LTL fragment into questions with predefined answers.
Use a System-One natural-language classifier to answer those questions.
Construct the LTL instruction from the predicted answers.
evidence_signal: Across three benchmarks, the translator matches or exceeds the accuracy of the best local LLMs evaluated, with up to an order-of-magnitude reduction in runtime and energy consumption, and generalizes to unseen atomic propositions and temporal patterns.
watch_item: Deployment should validate coverage of the supported LTL fragment and translation errors; formal task specifications alone do not guarantee that natural-language intent was captured correctly.
paper_title: Efficient Natural Language to Temporal Logic Translation for Real-Time Physical AI
